title: Thou, Infinite in Love
description: Thou, Infinite in Love in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Elizabeth Miles wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 333, “In Affliction”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou, in-fin-ite in love! Guide this be-wil-dered mind, Which, like the trem-bling dove, No rest-ing place can find On the wild wa-ters, God of light, Through the thick dark-ness lead me right!

lines: On the wild waters, — God of light,
Through the thick darkness lead me right!
As in the days gone by:
In Jesus' name I cry to Thee,
Fain would earth's true and dear
Save me in this dark hour;
And art not Thou more near?
Art Thou not love and power?
Vain is the help of man, — but Thou
There may be grief, and pain, and care
But, O my Father! Thou art there.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Elizabeth Miles died in 1877.
credits: Words by Sarah Elizabeth Miles (1807–1877), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
